relevance_note: Single case report of a man with a clinical (provisional) diagnosis of fish eye disease: 'Persistent hypoalphalipoproteinemia with characteristic corneal opacities led to the provisional diagnosis of fish eye disease'; no LCAT variant was identified because 'Genetic studies could not be performed'.
method_note: Read the short letter in full and built the JSON with a small script in my scratch directory. In scope by diagnosis (provisional, clinical diagnosis of fish eye disease), not by variant: genetic testing was not done, so the variants table is empty. Note that plasma LCAT activity was reported normal, which sits uneasily with the fish eye disease diagnosis; recorded as excluded 'reduced plasma LCAT activity'. Family members are mentioned only as a group ('Family members had no dyslipidemia or corneal opacities') with no individual-level detail, so they get no rows; the family-history statement about cardiovascular events and renal failure concerns relatives, not the patient, and was not used. Under D-27, 'renal function tests ... were normal' was recorded as excluded 'abnormal renal function tests', but the composite checklist item 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure' was left not reported; 'urine analysis ... normal' is a whole investigation and was not used to exclude proteinuria or hematuria. Statements that fish eye disease patients have no anemia or renal failure are general, not about this patient. Age 42 is the age at referral, recorded as age at last evaluation; no age at diagnosis or onset stated. n_patients_reported left null because no patient has a reported LCAT variant.
